newsitem.title: FRANCE: European space probe to analyse Saturn's moon.
newsitem.headline: European space probe to analyse Saturn's moon.

text.p: A group of European companies has built an interplanetary probe that will land on Saturn's largest moon after a seven-year journey through space and transmit information about its physical and chemical makeup back to Earth.

The Huygens probe, a 300 kg (660 lb) device named after the Dutch astronomer who discovered the moon, Titan, in 1655, will be launched next October in a joint mission with the U.S. space agency NASA, the French company Aerospatiale said on Wednesday.
Aerospatiale, the leader of the group of 13 European firms that made the probe, said it will be launched aboard a U.S. Titan IV Centaur rocket next October.

The probe will use the 'sling-shot' effect of the gravitational pull of the Earth, Venus and Jupiter to approach Saturn in 2004 and then land on Titan, whose chemistry and geology shows similarities to those of the Earth in its primitive stage.

As well as sending back scientific information, the Huygens probe will carry thousands of messages sent in by Internet users, ranging from calls for galactic peace to invitations to share a plate of pasta.
